relevance_note: Narrative 'How I Treat' review that gives only aggregate cohort frequencies ("Table 1 summarizes reported disease features using data from three published reviews") and no patient-level genotype or phenotype data for any individual.
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; no script transcribed any table (a script only assembled and checked the JSON). Table 1 gives only per-cohort percentages from cited reviews/cohorts (refs 3, 4, 21, 22/27, 21, 23-26) with no individual patients, so no individuals, variants or phenotype rows were emitted. The only single patient mentioned is an anecdote with no label, sex, age or variant: "In one severe and refractory case, we have referred a patient for allogeneic stem cell transplantation, who has been in drug-free remission for over 2 years after transplant." It was not emitted as an individual because no genetic or other individual-level information is given. n_patients_reported left null: the paper gives only aggregate counts from other sources (e.g. "to date ∼200 cases have been reported worldwide"; Table 1 columns of 199, 177, 54, 12 and 185 patients with "Some overlap exists between cohorts"), not a count of patients described in this document. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null because the document describes no patients of its own; it does draw Table 1 data from the authors' own published multicenter cohort ("an international multicenter cohort from our group describing 185 cases assessed longitudinally in 41 clinics and seven countries (22)"). Contradiction noted inside the paper: the text cites the multicenter cohort of 185 cases as reference (22), but the Table 1 column header labels it "Multicenter cohort (27)"; reference 27 is a different 2020 paper. Reference 63 is listed but not cited in the text.
